newsitem.title: USA: N.J. eyes pension funds for 1998 budget -- paper.
newsitem.headline: N.J. eyes pension funds for 1998 budget -- paper.

text.p: Gov Christine Whitman is looking into whether New Jersey can find more "efficiencies" in the state's pension system as part of her effort to develop a budget for fiscal 1998, the Star Ledger reported Thursday.
The newspaper, citing an interview with Whitman and state Treasurer Brian Clymer, said the budget for the fiscal year beginning July 1 would be light on layoffs and heavy on one-shot revenue raisers.

Specific details about pension fund changes or proposed one-shots were not available, but Whitman said she does not expect any large tax cuts. Whitman, a Republican who is seeking reelection in November, attracted national attention by cutting state income taxes a total of 30 percent since taking office in 1994.
A large part of the revenues lost to tax decreases were replaced by cuts in state funding of pension funds, a move that prompted criticism and lawsuits from labor leaders.
One-shot proposals, which may include asset sales, could be as much as five percent of revenues in the new budget, Whitman said in her interview with the newspaper.
